run.procedureSummary: Start: q=[3,6,6,2,2,1], all LARVAL, loss=0. Each cycle 1-5, in order: (1) Feed: add the cycle's table row to every chamber regardless of state or capacity. (2) Carry: for i=1..6 in sequence, if q[i]>cap[i], move q[i]-cap[i] into chamber i+1 (which may then itself exceed capacity and pass on in its own turn); chamber 6's excess goes to loss. (3) Check, on post-carry quantities: LARVAL with q>=upper becomes PUPAL; PUPAL with q<=lower becomes LARVAL; otherwise unchanged; each change logged (cycle, position, before, after). (4) Metabolise, using post-check states and quantities, all shares computed first then applied together: LARVAL loses floor(q/4) to loss; PUPAL loses floor(q/2), which goes to chamber i-1 (chamber 1's share goes to loss). Any resulting overfill is left in place for the next cycle's carry. (5) Moult: if the six-chamber total after metabolise is strictly greater than 38, each chamber keeps floor(q/2) and the remainder goes to loss; cycle logged. States are not re-checked after metabolise or moult.

openPoints.assumption: Sequential left to right in one pass; a chamber's received overflow counts in its own turn, so overflow can cascade down the line to chamber 6 and out.
Upper is inclusive (q >= upper turns LARVAL to PUPAL); lower is inclusive (q <= lower turns PUPAL back to LARVAL). A chamber changes at most once per check.
The state just set by that cycle's check.
All shares (quarter burn, half pass, half kept on moult) rounded down per chamber; on moult the chamber keeps floor(q/2) and the discarded part is q - floor(q/2).
LARVAL burn, chamber 6 carry excess, chamber 1 PUPAL half, and moult discards all go to the loss tally; PUPAL half from chamber i>1 goes into chamber i-1 even if it exceeds capacity.
Total measured after metabolise; fires only when strictly over 38. Cycle 5 ends at exactly 38, so no moult in cycle 5.
No carry after cycle 5, so chamber 2 ends at 10 against capacity 8 and it is reported as is.
Not re-checked; end states are the cycle 5 check states.
